Most recently, Merrigan and colleagues (55) randomized recreationally active women to perform 3 to 4 sets of the squat and leg press either as compound sets or using a traditional approach. For the compound sets, subjects performed the squat and leg press in immediate succession, then rested for 140 to 150 seconds before performing the next compound set; the traditional group performed sets of squats and then the leg press with 1-minute rest intervals. Increases in muscle thickness and cross-sectional area were similar between conditions, indicating that compound sets neither hinder nor enhance muscular adaptations.
